title: PolicyTest
description:
A `.zitadel/policies/<operation>.test.json` file: cases `zitadel policies
test` evaluates against the policy in the sibling `<operation>.json`, or
against the one a release pins. Each case states the operation's input
and, where it matters, the facts the operation would look up, and the
decision it expects. The server evaluates every case
(`POST /policies/evaluate`); `zitadel deploy` does not carry test files.

$schema.description: Editor affordance: path or URL of this schema so editors validate and autocomplete the file (policy test files point at `.zitadel/meta/policy-test.json`). Ignored by the platform.

PolicyTestPasswordSet.title: PasswordSetPolicyTest
PolicyTestPasswordSet.description: Test cases for the password policy, checked before a password is set.

operation.description: The operation whose policy the cases test.

name.description: What the case shows, printed with its result.

PasswordSetEvaluateInput.title: PasswordSetEvaluateInput
PasswordSetEvaluateInput.description:
The password as a user or administrator would set it. The server derives
what the policy checks (its length in code points after NFC normalization)
with the same code a password set runs.

password.description:
The candidate password. It is evaluated and dropped: never stored,
logged or returned.

PasswordSetEvaluateFacts.title: PasswordSetEvaluateFacts
PasswordSetEvaluateFacts.description:
What a password set looks up instead of reading from the request. A dry run
has no user, so it is stated here.

self_service.description:
Whether the user sets their own password. Only then is the password
history checked; an administrator's set skips it.

history_matches.description:
Whether the candidate matches each of the user's kept passwords,
current first, newest first. Only the first `history_depth` entries
count.

PolicyTestExpect.title: PolicyTestExpect
PolicyTestExpect.description:
The decision a case expects. `code` and `violations` are checked only when
given.

allowed.description: Whether the operation should go ahead.

code.description:
The error code the operation should refuse with, as the live operation
answers it, for example `user.password_empty`.

violations.description:
The names of exactly the rules that should fail, for example
`["min_length"]`.
